events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: West Side Mountains South of 198; Buttonwillow - Lost Hills - I5; Buena Vista; Bakersfield; South End San Joaquin Valley; Kern River Valley; Piute Walker Basin; Tehachapi; Grapevine; Frazier Mountain Communities; Indian Wells Valley; Mojave Desert Slopes; Mojave Desert
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall from storms
training over the same area.

* WHERE...A portion of central California, including the following
areas, Bakersfield, Buena Vista, Buttonwillow - Lost Hills - I5,
Frazier Mountain Communities, Grapevine, Indian Wells Valley, Kern
River Valley, Mojave Desert, Mojave Desert Slopes, Piute Walker
Basin, South End San Joaquin Valley, Tehachapi and West Side
Mountains South of 198.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become
clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Strong area of low pressure off the Southern California coast
will move inland and interact with tropical moisture.
- Be especially careful on Highway 58 between mile markers 101 to
103 and the Borel burn scar.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHEN...Until 11 AM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely

Highway/Pass.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Southwest San Juan Mountains; Four Corners/Upper Dolores River; Animas River Basin; San Juan River Basin; Southeast Utah; Arches/Grand Flat; La Sal and Abajo Mountains; Canyonlands/Natural Bridges
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and Utah,
including the following areas, Arches/Grand Flat,
Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains and
Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...Through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recent burn scars and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Strong thunderstorms capable of producing heavy rain will be
possible across southern portions of Utah and Colorado through
Thursday evening. In addition widespread moderate to heavy
rainfall from a surge of tropical moisture will remain a threat
through early Friday morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
At 1027 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong
thunderstorms extending from 16 miles west of Shiprock to 5 miles
north of Crystal, moving northeast at 40 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Shiprock, Sanostee, Newcomb, Toadlena, Sheep Springs, Narbona Pass,
Crystal, Tocito, Rattlesnake and Naschitti.

This includes Highway 64 between Mile Markers 1 and 29 as well as
U.S. Highway 491.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest New Mexico, including the following
areas, Eastern Black Range Foothills, Southern Gila
Foothills/Mimbres Valley and Southwest Desert/Lower Gila River
Valley.

* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An incoming potent upper level system coupled with abnormally
high moisture will allow for scattered to numerous thunderstorms
Thursday afternoon, evening and into Friday morning. Storms will
be efficient rain makers which could lead to flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
